cases.brief:
Determinism pins and a stability loop for screenshots (CTX-1183) (#627)

* Determinism pins and a stability loop for screenshots (CTX-1183)

The play runner pins each page: a fixed origin (http://localhost:6006,
routed to the real server), a Date that starts at a fixed time and runs,
and a seeded Math.random. Each story gets its own browser context. Chromium
starts with partial raster off, because partial raster anti-aliased rounded
corners differently from run to run.

When a story ends, the runner settles the page: no CSS animation, no
transition, no text caret, and the web fonts loaded. The story Testing/Play
host checks each pin and fails when one is missing.

A story without a play function ends in the "completed" phase, so the
capture can shoot it. The capture takes shots until two in a row are the
same (at most 4), else the status is "unstable". The nightly CI run
captures 100 stories two times (job "Screenshot determinism").


* Wait for completed before a shot, pause between shots, place popovers again (CTX-1183)

A capture ends each story at the completed phase, so Storybook waits for the
running animations first. A story with a play must still reach played. After
a shot that differs, the capture waits 250 ms before the next shot (at most 6
shots). The settle step sends a resize event, so that a popover that measured
a moving trigger is placed again.


* Drop source-text tests and inline the start time (CTX-1183)

The tests that matched the runner source and the workflow text checked no
behavior, so they go. The start time of the page clock is used in one place
and moves there. The screenshot no longer hides the caret itself: the settle
step does it.


* Set the end phase from the capture hook (CTX-1183)

Only a capture plays a story without a play function, so the end phase
follows from afterPlay. The exported helper and its tests go.


* Fix the shot limit inside the stability loop (CTX-1183)


* Prove the seed of Math.random with a new frame (CTX-1183)

Each new frame starts the seeded generator, so the play-host story checks
the first two values of a new frame. An unseeded wrapper now fails it.


* Skip the known unstable stories in the determinism proof (CTX-1183)

scripts/ci/visual-unstable-stories.json lists 9 stories that still differ
between two runs, each with a reason and a ticket. The proof and the nightly
job report them as skipped. Any other story that differs still fails.

cases.brief:
Workspace settings as one card for each part, with the live work in the sources (#529)

* Make the default link teal, not blue

DESIGN.md makes teal the one link accent and allows no second accent.
The primary variant of the shared Link component was blue, so each
link that used the default was blue. It is now teal: teal-400 on the
dark product floor, teal-300 on hover.

Other blue in the UI is not a link and does not change here: the
AlertDialog icon, the ListBox and TagGroup selection, ProgressBar, and
the chat status spinner.


* Add a Switch component

An on/off setting that applies at once, with its label on the right. It
uses the React Aria Switch, the focus ring of the other controls, and
teal for "on". The automatic upgrades setting of Workspace settings is
its first user.


* Workspace settings as one card for each part, with the live work in the sources

Workspace settings showed the state of a Workspace in several places:
status tags in the header, a Status group with a headline, and an
"Ingesting now" list that repeated the sources below it without their
state. A user could not see at once what needed them or what ran.

Each part of the Workspace is now a card: Upgrades, Sources, Knowledge
graph, Repository, Workspace, and Danger zone. Each card states its
state one time, in its body, and holds its own settings and actions.
A line at the top names the parts that need the user and the parts at
work, with a link to each card. A card that needs the user has an
amber edge. A link to #upgrades still lands on the Upgrades card.

Upgrades:
- Each upgrade that needs the user or runs now is a row with a dot.
  Its facts are in one muted line, and its action is a small button on
  the right of the title. Each row keeps its own start and check.
- Automatic upgrades is a switch with one line of help.
- The format shows as "Format 3, the latest", with a tooltip that says
  what a format is.
- History shows the five newest upgrades. "Show all" shows the rest in
  a scroll area. Each row opens to its description, check, spend,
  steps, and reports.
- The card shows no cost estimate, as CTX-894 decided.

Sources:
- Each source shows its live work in its own row: the word of the run
  that is the furthest (for example "Publishing"), and its time. "N
  runs" opens each run with its stage, its count, a bar, and why it
  waits. The separate "Ingesting now" list is gone.
- A source with a problem shows the problem, also while it syncs. The
  live work then shows under the row.
- Each connector is an accordion. It opens by itself when it works,
  needs attention, or waits for a merge. Headers, rows, and runs share
  one column grid, so the dots, the times, and the actions line up.
- The create form and the setup guide keep the table layout.

Knowledge graph: the hydrate state, the error of a failed hydrate, the
indexing of the newest commit, the projection lag, and the skipped
files, in one card.

Repository: write access is one line with its fix. A problem keeps the

Workspace settings as one card for each part, with the live work in the sources (#529)

* Make the default link teal, not blue

The primary variant of the shared Link component was blue, so each
link that used the default was blue. It is now teal: teal-400 on the
dark product floor, teal-300 on hover.

Other blue in the UI is not a link and does not change here: the
AlertDialog icon, the ListBox and TagGroup selection, ProgressBar, and
the chat status spinner.


* Add a Switch component

An on/off setting that applies at once, with its label on the right. It
uses the React Aria Switch, the focus ring of the other controls, and
teal for "on". The automatic upgrades setting of Workspace settings is
its first user.


* Workspace settings as one card for each part, with the live work in the sources

Workspace settings showed the state of a Workspace in several places:
status tags in the header, a Status group with a headline, and an
"Ingesting now" list that repeated the sources below it without their
state. A user could not see at once what needed them or what ran.

Each part of the Workspace is now a card: Upgrades, Sources, Knowledge
graph, Repository, Workspace, and Danger zone. Each card states its
state one time, in its body, and holds its own settings and actions.
A line at the top names the parts that need the user and the parts at
work, with a link to each card. A card that needs the user has an
amber edge. A link to #upgrades still lands on the Upgrades card.

- Each upgrade that needs the user or runs now is a row with a dot.
  Its facts are in one muted line, and its action is a small button on
  the right of the title. Each row keeps its own start and check.
- Automatic upgrades is a switch with one line of help.
- The format shows as "Format 3, the latest", with a tooltip that says
  what a format is.
- History shows the five newest upgrades. "Show all" shows the rest in
  a scroll area. Each row opens to its description, check, spend,
  steps, and reports.
- The card shows no cost estimate, as CTX-894 decided.

- Each source shows its live work in its own row: the word of the run
  that is the furthest (for example "Publishing"), and its time. "N
  runs" opens each run with its stage, its count, a bar, and why it
  waits. The separate "Ingesting now" list is gone.
- A source with a problem shows the problem, also while it syncs. The
  live work then shows under the row.
- Each connector is an accordion. It opens by itself when it works,
  needs attention, or waits for a merge. Headers, rows, and runs share
  one column grid, so the dots, the times, and the actions line up.
- The create form and the setup guide keep the table layout.

indexing of the newest commit, the projection lag, and the skipped
files, in one card.

Repository: write access is one line with its fix. A problem keeps the
title and the facts of the alert that it replaces, and is an alert.

removed. groupSourceRuns has unit tests. The stories of the pane, the

Slack connector: intent-based thread capture (#267)

* Add Slack connection schema and encrypted bot token config.

Introduce connections.type=slack, draft channel/sync-target/dirty-thread tables, and AES-GCM bot token storage so OAuth and sync can land on a typed foundation.

* Add Slack OAuth, channel listing, and Events webhook intake.

Wire deployment-owned Slack app OAuth with encrypted bot tokens, admin connector routes for status/available-channels, and a signed Events endpoint that marks dirty threads for later coalesced flush.

* Add Slack config PR, thread mirror sync, and dirty flush workflows.

Implement slack/config.yaml review flow, thread-first Markdown conversion with capped file downloads, backfill after merge, and Events-driven dirty-thread flushes on a ~5 minute coalescing cadence.

* Add Slack connector setup UI and OAuth relay route.

Wire catalog entry, connection card, channel/sync-target wizard, and
/.slack/setup popup fallback into the connectors page.

* Document self-hosted Slack app setup and env vars.

Cover OAuth callback, Events URL, bot scopes, and channel opt-in for
operators deploying one Slack app per ctxpipe instance.

* Honor Slack quiet period with flush sleep retries.

Flush workflows that find dirty-but-not-ready threads sleep until the
earliest quiet/max-lag deadline instead of exiting empty under a 5-minute
idempotency key.

* Wire optional Slack credentials into aws-cdk connector secrets.

Self-hosted ECS can inject SLACK_CLIENT_ID/SECRET and SLACK_SIGNING_SECRET
the same way as GitHub and Atlassian connector env.

* Record Slack connector git-native mirror pattern in memory.

Capture deployment-owned app, config PR, quiet-period flush, and
private-channel opt-in defaults for future agents.

* Complete Slack merge/reset path and regression coverage.

Load slack/config.yaml on GitHub push, reset to draft when it is
removed, and cover workflow discovery, YAML stability, and the
partial-failure delete guard.

* Wire hosted Slack app secrets through Terraform and CI.

Inject SLACK_CLIENT_* and SLACK_SIGNING_SECRET into Railway backend/worker
env only when all three values are non-empty, avoiding empty-string parseEnv
failures.

* Document Slack connector product flow and accept ADR-022.

Add source-connector and context-repository docs, extend ADR-018's type set,
and point AGENTS.md at the Slack connection model.

* Add Storybook coverage for Slack connector catalog and cards.

MSW status handlers cover live, awaiting-merge, and loading card states plus
the catalog entry.

* Pass Slack secrets and AUTH_SECRET into Compose deploy services.

Backend and worker both need Slack app env and decryption keys for
OAuth/Events and OpenWorkflow sync; empty values coerce to unset in parseEnv.

* Harden Slack sync for rate limits, deletes, and multi-tenant Events.

Retry Slack API 429/5xx, delete empty/deleted thread trees on flush, fan out
Events by teamId to every matching connection, retry rate-limited backfills,
and start content sync when config already matches but setup is not live.

* Keep Slack setup dialog mounted outside the catalog modal.

Closing the add-connection catalog was unmounting the setup dialog, so
Slack appeared to open and immediately close.

* Drop unused MSW imports from Slack add-button story.

* Improve Slack setup UX: stepper, docs link, channel empty state.

Reuse the shared connector stepper, link product docs, explain bot-invite
empty channels, and list membership via users.conversations.

* Align Slack setup dialog styling with Notion and Confluence.

Drop the boxed empty states and native form chrome; reuse shared field
components and the same list/typography patterns as the other connectors.

* Harden Slack lifecycle and setup UX.

Keep incomplete syncs out of the live state, gate events until setup completes, and make the connector flow expose its asynchronous progress.

* Align Slack setup with proven connector patterns.

Use GitHub defaults and staged setup screens while making Slack channel discovery explicit about invitation requirements and upstream failures.

* Complete Slack repository handoff and stabilise channel selection.

* Prioritise existing GitHub installation org on setup callbacks.

* Support Slack config PRs for empty repositories.

Port the Notion GitHub writer path so empty sync-target repos get initialised before branch creation, and surface a retry when PR creation fails instead of a false "still running" state.

* Harden Slack setup recovery and preview syncs.

* Harden connector completion handling and self-hosting guidance.

* Close Slack connector race and webhook review blockers.

Bind webhook processing to authenticated connections and make config/sync state transitions resilient under concurrency.

* Fix Slack dirty-thread flush durability.

Delete stale thread assets, preserve dirty rows when guarded deletes are suppressed, and fail unsuccessful workflow steps so OpenWorkflow retries them.

* Pivot Slack connector from channel mirror to intent capture.

Replace continuous Events/backfill with app_mention thread snapshots into the
context repo, in-thread capturing→captured status, and docs that pair the
connector with Slack MCP for general workspace access.

* Allow Slack to bind context repos without a repositories-page detour.

Match Notion/Linear create-on-bind so selecting a GitHub App repo (or newly created ctxpipe-context) registers it and goes live in one step.

* Recover Slack setup when a deleted connectionId is still cached.

After remove/uninstall, the setup dialog kept polling status with a stale id (404), which blocked Connect Slack. Reset on open and offer Start over.

* Stop downloading Slack attachments; link them and shorten capture status.

Align Slack capture with Notion/Linear by stubbing file permalinks in markdown, and replace the raw repo path status with a View in GitHub link.

* Let a new Slack mention recapture the same thread.

Idempotency is now per mention timestamp so Slack retries still dedupe, but a later @ writes a fresh snapshot instead of silently no-oping.

* Document Slack attachments as permalink stubs, not git binaries.

Product and self-host docs still described the old download-into-assets path; capture now links Slack permalinks only.

* Document Slack self-host landmines that block capture and indexing.

Call out Socket Mode, reinstall dropping channel membership, handle vs display name, and that GitHub push webhooks must hit this deployment before the UI indexes.

* Point Slack code comments at ADR-024 instead of Linear's ADR-022.

Slack intent capture lives in ADR-024; leftover 022 citations were copy-paste from the Linear connector.

* Cap Slack thread snapshots at 500 messages.

Stops unbounded conversations.replies pagination on mega-threads so the shared hosted Slack app cannot be quota-exhausted by one capture.

* Drop the implied Slack capture phrase; a mention is enough.

Product docs and the setup dialog no longer suggest a required 'please capture this thread' incantation.

* feat(slack): mention agent, unique workspace, auditable capture

Route app_mention through a small in-thread agent with a capture_thread
tool instead of always snapshotting and ignoring mention text. Bare
mention or capture intent writes git; other intents get a capability
reply. Recapture overwrites the same thread path with handle+name
provenance, permalink, and captured_at.

Enforce one Slack teamId per ctx| org, revoke on uninstall, reject DMs,
always settle in-thread status, and drop legacy GitHub webhook secret
fallback. Docs and setup UI now use the installed bot handle and
auditable (not reviewed) positioning.


* refactor(slack): store capture binding on connections.config

Drop leftover Confluence-shaped slack_sync_targets. Slack now keeps
repositoryId/branch/enabled on connections.config like Linear/Notion,
derives setupPhase, clears the binding on repo delete, and enqueues
ingestion when bind creates a context repo.


* fix(slack): always publish a terminal mention status

Fall back to a new thread reply when chat.update of the working message
fails or never posted, and post a failure (or 503) when enqueue itself
fails so Slack never stays on "working…" or goes silent.


* refactor(slack): squash unreleased migrations to the teamId unique index

The five Slack migrations on this branch created then dropped
slack_channels, slack_dirty_threads, and slack_sync_targets. None of
those tables exist on main, so regenerate a single CREATE UNIQUE INDEX
for connections_slack_team_id_uq.


* fix(slack): create teamId unique index only if missing

The PR Neon branch already applied the pre-squash migration that created connections_slack_team_id_uq, so the replacement CREATE UNIQUE INDEX was failing with 42P07.

* fix(slack): ACK Events before enqueue so Slack retries do not kill the worker

Awaiting OpenWorkflow on the webhook path overran Slack's ~3s budget, produced 499s, and stacked Railway wakes. Return 200 first, widen wake debounce, and record the live-debug lessons.

* docs: stop listing shipped Slack, Linear, and Notion as unavailable

FAQ, connection overview, and README still treated those connectors as coming soon. Point self-host links at Linear and Notion until the hosted Notion guide lands separately.

* fix(slack): refuse capture unless the mention is in a thread

Channel-top-level app_mention has no thread_ts; collapsing to the mention ts
was snapshotting the invocation. Reply in-thread and skip enqueue.
